title: What to wear
description:
Write a function that gives clothing advice from the temperature and whether it is raining.

```
advice(25, false)  ->  "T-shirt weather"
advice(12, true)   ->  "Jacket and an umbrella"
advice(-3, false)  ->  "Coat, hat and gloves"
```
hints: Test the ranges from the top down, so each `else if` needs only one comparison: `if (celsius >= 25)`, `else if (celsius >= 15)`, and so on.
Keep the result in a `let` and add the umbrella at the end with `+=` or a template literal (lesson 1.04).
requirements: `advice(celsius, raining)` returns a string: 25 or more `T-shirt weather`, 15 to 24 `A light jumper`, 5 to 14 `Jacket`, below 5 `Coat, hat and gloves`.
When it is raining, add ` and an umbrella` to the end.
A value that is not a number (`typeof`, `Number.isNaN`) returns `"Not a temperature"`.
stretch: Accept Fahrenheit too, with a third parameter `unit` that defaults to `"C"` (look up default parameters, `function advice(celsius, raining, unit = "C")`, in lesson 2.01).
